週.meaning: A runner does one <part>lap</part> of the track each day, then rolls down the <part>ramp</part> counting out loud: Monday, Tuesday... When she says Sunday she reaches the bottom: one whole <kanji>week</kanji>.
週.on: At the bottom the runner kicks off a <sound>shoe</sound>, one for each day of the week.

先.meaning: A mound of <part>soil</part> with a <part>slash</part> of weed sticking out of it grows a pair of <part>legs</part> and races everyone to the finish line. It always gets there first, long <kanji>before</kanji> the rest.
先.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try at the finish line salutes the muddy winner.
先.kun: It crosses the line ahead of a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a brass <sound>key</sound>, both still running.

地.meaning: A <part>scorpion</part> scuttles across the <part>soil</part> and digs in its tail. It burrows down and down until it hits solid rock: the hard <kanji>ground</kanji> under everything.
地.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah sprints over the ground, and the scorpion pops back up to watch it pass.

士.meaning: Flip a mound of <part>soil</part> upside down and you get this: a wide brim on top, a short neat base below, a straight post in between. It tips its brim to everyone and holds every door. It's a <kanji>gentleman</kanji>.
士.on: He holds up a polished <sound>shi</sound>eld to keep the rain off strangers.
士.kun: He serves <sound>sa</sound>shimi, a cow says '<sound>Mu</sound>!', and he slices <sound>rye</sound> bread with his long sword.

売.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> stands on a folded <part>blanket</part> draped over a pair of <part>legs</part>. His helper underneath walks him down the street while he shouts: 'Blankets! Warm blankets!' Everything must go. He wants to <kanji>sell</kanji>.
売.on: He sells the last blanket and buys a shiny <sound>bi</sound>ke with the money.
売.kun: '<sound>Ooh</sound>!' says a buyer, stroking the soft blanket.

会.meaning: Rain pours. Two strangers dash under the same <part>umbrella</part>, their <part>kite</part> strings tangled together below it. By the time they've untangled them and the rain stops, they've swapped names and phone numbers. A lucky <kanji>meeting</kanji>.
会.on: Then the wind snatches the umbrella, and it flies off like a <sound>ki</sound>te.
会.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, hello again!' they both say, when they bump into each other a week later.
